ki.$description: Reduced transparency (spec 044): every surface that holds content becomes the opaque surface its glass or tint reads as over the page, and nothing blurs what is behind it. References only, so one file serves every theme and scheme. The semantic tint ramp (`surface.*-alpha`) is left alone because state washes draw from it: washes, disabled fills and the modal scrim keep their alpha (spec 044 D1); content tints have their own tokens (`surface.*-tint`), remapped here.

blur-base-light.$description: Glass panel (listbox, tooltip, dialog start stop) as an opaque surface: the page white in light, the s3 step a translucent dark-700 panel resolves to in dark.

blur-base-dark.$description: Denser glass panel as the same opaque surface as blur-base-light.

secondary-alpha-base.$description: Secondary glass (secondary button, neutral badge, avatar-group counter) as the opaque s2 it tints in light and s3 in dark.

primary-tint.$description: The primary content tint as the opaque primary-low-em surface of the same tone and emphasis.

info-tint.$description: The info content tint as the opaque info-base-em surface of the same tone and emphasis.

success-tint.$description: The success content tint as the opaque success-base-em surface of the same tone and emphasis.

warning-tint.$description: The warning content tint as the opaque warning-base-em surface of the same tone and emphasis.

danger-tint.$description: The danger content tint as the opaque danger-base-em surface of the same tone and emphasis.

backdrop-blur.$description: No backdrop blur behind glass components: their fills are opaque.
No backdrop blur behind the opaque listbox.
